headline: Palantir chief executive Alex Karp said that only people with vocational training or neurodivergence can count on a future in the age of AI.
score_reason: Pool 5 lowered by 2: old news; the remarks were made in March 2026 and Fortune republished its 24 Mar story on 10 Oct.
importance_line: Workers choosing careers hear one executive's blunt view of who will keep a future, which touches students and young job-seekers first, then employers; it is one chief executive's opinion from March, other tech leaders disagree, and the story is a republished one.
summary: Fortune reports, in a story first published on 24 Mar 2026 and republished on 10 Oct, that Alex Karp, chief executive of the data-analysis company Palantir, said on the TBPN show in March that people have a future in the AI era only if they have 'some vocational training' or are neurodivergent, a term that includes dyslexia, ADHD and autism; Karp has spoken of his own dyslexia. Fortune sets this against Microsoft chief scientist Jaime Teevan and Anthropic co-founder Daniela Amodei, who say critical thinking and the humanities will matter more, and notes that Palantir runs fellowships aimed at neurodivergent recruits and at school-leavers who skip college.
notes: Re-dated old news: Karp's TBPN remarks are from March 2026 (exact day not stated) and Fortune's own text says a version was first published 24 Mar 2026. Expect it to be held back as stale.
